pydantic strict order-intent schema in place of the hand-written order-contract checks
overturn_protocol.metric: Count of failed lifecycle cases on the same frozen inputs and failure contract (ambiguous submit, duplicate/restart, partial/cancel, stale quote/clock, request budget, ownership, kill/STOP), plus pass/fail of fresh cash/position reconciliation after a bounded open-session paper trial

overturn_when:
Any of the following would change this verdict:
- An open-session adaptive paper trial run through blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/runner.py (paper, then recover) fails ownership, fresh cash/position reconciliation or numeric-risk enforcement.
- Induced partial-fill, cancel-race, stream-loss or ambiguous-submit faults in that runner (currently covered only by tests/test_adaptive_paper_safety.py and tests/test_adaptive_paper_recovery.py) are not handled.
- The Nautilus IBKR adapter (c7) passes the same ownership, reconciliation and partial/cancel/reconnect cases in a real paper session while c5 does not.
- A non-adopted challenger (HKUDS/Vibe-Trading's order gate, or a pydantic strict order-intent schema) is executed against the existing lifecycle cases in tests/test_alpaca_paper.py and tests/test_order_contract.py and produces fewer failures than the current deterministic adapter and hand-written boundary.
why_selected:
c5 is selected because it is the only adopted candidate whose retained evidence places a broker-specific boundary inside the selected NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 destination. c4 (alpaca-py 0.44.0) is selected as the official SDK that carries c5's transport. It is also the only adopted broker component with a retained broker-observed paper order result.

What the retained evidence shows, from my reading of the receipts (I did not re-run anything):

c5 (adaptive-paper-alpaca-adapter):
- blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/receipt.json records status "local_integration_passed_new_broker_trial_pending" and pins NautilusTrader 1b0a49d2 and alpaca-py cc4cb3b7.
- The same receipt records 42 unchanged upstream Nautilus adapter-template tests passed, scoped "not Alpaca broker E2E".
- It records a full repository suite of 895 run, 893 passed and 2 skipped.
- It records a wall-clock native-engine capacity fixture with a synthetic broker: 180 submissions, 90 roundtrips, broker_connections 0 and paper_orders 0.
- The execution_contract block holds the deterministic numeric risk limits: 5000 USD gross exposure, 1000 USD order notional, 25 USD loss/drawdown, 200/180 per-minute request budgets and 1x maximum leverage. It also records a durable SQLite intent/fill/request journal and reconciliation-based recovery.
- blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/README.md (Lifecycle and native boundaries) describes fsync-before-send reservations, stable IDs, an account lock, a flat-start requirement and snapshot reconciliation. It says ambiguous POSTs are never blindly retried.
- The later changes_since* blocks are all labelled evidence class SYN and are explicitly "not a new broker E2E".
- broker_readiness is "not_started" (regular_session_window_unavailable).

c4 (alpaca-py):
- blueprints/us-equities/paper-e2e-20260921/paper-receipt.json records a native Alpaca paper SPY long-to-flat trial through the SDK, with SDK source hashes for alpaca/trading/client.py.
- It observed 2 write attempts, both filled, and a realized gross PnL of -0.08 USD.
- A separate fresh read-only reconciliation passed with positions 0, open orders 0 and a cash delta of -0.08 matching the PnL.
- Completed-trial recovery made 0 additional writes.
- blueprints/us-equities/order-contract/README.md records a network-isolated native probe of alpaca-py 0.44.0 serialization. The SDK uses float fields and silently drops advanced_instructions and unknown fields, which is why the project wraps it in a strict offline boundary.

Evidence class: the winner set is local_integration, the weaker of the two. c5 has only local integration and synthetic evidence. The one native paper result belongs to a separate runner (blueprints/us-equities/alpaca-paper/paper_runner.py), not to c5.
